newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian budget should not depress demand - Fazio.
newsitem.headline: Italian budget should not depress demand - Fazio.

text.p: The 1997 budget should not depress demand, but it will cut disposable income, Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said on Tuesday.
The government budget aims to slash 62.5 trillion lire off next year's projected deficit through a mix of spending cuts, new revenue raising measures and Treasury operations.

"The proposed spending cuts are an important step towards eliminating waste and the rent positions hidden in the crannies of the public accounts. They should not depress demand," Fazio told a conference organised by Euromoney.
"Overall, the budget can be expected to result in the private sector's disposable income rising by around two percent, compared with a pre-budget forecast of around five percent," he added.
Fazio said the tough budget package, annnounced at the end of September, had caused a substantial fall in market rates.

"The decline underway in market interest rates will result in a much larger gain for public finances than that implicit in the estimates published in the...September Forecasting and Planning Report," Fazio said.
Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said last week the government had already chalked up savings of five trillion lire for next year due to the fall in rates.
Fazio told Wednesday's conference that Italy had made a serious start on reducing the budget deficit in relation to gross domestic product (GDP).
However, he said there now needed to be urgent action to boost the economy in the south and to encourage investment.

"In the shorter term, the resources required to finance a larger volume of investment can be made available mainly through further adjustments serving to complete the consolidation of the public finances," Fazio said.
"Budgetary efforts will have to focus on reducing expenditure through strucutural reforms able to ensure lasting equilibrium," he added. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
